title: MSFS 2024 Scenic Coastal Gateways & Challenging Regional Airfields
description:
The Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 marketplace just exploded with an incredibly diverse set of releases this week, bringing a massive mix of high-fidelity regional fields, scenic coastal getaways, and stunning visual landmarks. If you're tired of the same old standard global hops and want to put your stick and rudder skills to the test, this week's drop covers an incredible amount of ground across both Europe and North America, pushing away from sprawling multi-runway mega hubs.

In this comprehensive marketplace breakdown, we are putting the biggest new releases head-to-head against the default MSFS 2024 streaming engine to analyze the structural upgrades, custom terminal interior details, and night illumination overhauls to see which add-ons genuinely deserve a spot in your virtual hangar.

To make sense of this massive drop, we have organized the latest releases into two logical categories:

✈️ MAINLINE COASTAL GATEWAYS: We kick off with prominent coastal airliner getaways, heading straight to Nice Côte d'Azur Airport (LFMN) by France VFR. We evaluate its photorealistic 3D buildings and custom night lighting side-by-side against the default MSFS 2024 streaming engine. Next, we journey to Germany to explore Dortmund Airport (EDLW) by Salvuz to look at its highly detailed terminal interior with walking passengers, before heading down under to Queensland, Australia to visit Toowoomba Wellcamp Airport (YBWW)—featuring 1-meter DAM high-quality terrain data and a runway big enough for the Queen of the Skies!

🇬🇧 REGIONAL & SHORT-FIELD NETWORK: For the short-field pilots, we shift focus to challenging regional environments. We check out the beautifully elevated cliffside runway of Kalymnos Island National Airport (LGKY) by MM Simulations in Greece. Then, we cross the Atlantic to tackle the crosswinds at Yampa Valley Regional Airport (KHDN) by V Pilot Designs in Colorado, before wrapping up at Dundee Airport (EGPN) in Scotland to see how the UK2000 scenery library integration transforms this classic Eastern Scotland gateway.

Are you going to be taking a heavy commercial jet liner down to the French Riviera, practicing your short-field arrivals over in Greece, or pulling out a turboprop to tackle the winds in Scotland? Let me know in the comments below: which of these packages is landing on your hard drive first?

If this structured marketplace breakdown helps you plan your next flight route, make sure to hit that like button and subscribe for weekly MSFS realism updates!
